transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-26 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 mins
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (CTO, Meridian), Dana Park (Security Eng), Omar Khalil (Infra Lead), Jesse Meyers (Product), short intro from Legal (unnamed)

Summary (auto): quick security posture intake to validate requirements for inference hosting. Main asks: BYOK, audit log retention ~1 year, SSO via SAML + SCIM, RBAC groups mapping, SOC2 evidence.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i'm alex from redwood inference, i'll kick us off. um quick agenda — high level security Qs, then priya will do a short architecture sketch, then we collect requirements and next steps.
00:18 Luis Ortega: yep, thanks alex. we've been evaluating some vendors, want to make sure we cover the compliance and ops bits — soc two, key management, and how RBAC maps to our idp.
00:30 Alex Chen: totally; background for the team — redwood supports hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private (vpc or on prem). priya will talk through network and key options.
00:45 Priya Nair: hi all — quick note, i might mispronounce a few cloud names, sorry in advance. our private option is essentially customer-controlled control plane that sits in your vpc, optional on-prem appliance for air gap. we offer bring your own key via customer KMS integrations (aws-kms, gcp-kms, azure-key-vault) and we have hsm hooks for the private path.
01:05 Dana Park: when you say BYOK, is that full disk/at-rest keying for model weights, or just the metadata and customer data? we need everything encrypted with our key for regulatory reasons.
01:18 Priya Nair: good question. hosted supports provider-managed keys by default but we offer a BYOK flow for Dedicated and Private. for BYOK the keys are in your KMS and we use envelope encryption so your customer keys wrap the data keys; the K V cache and token storage are encrypted under that envelope. note on hosted with BYOK there are additional network controls — some customers choose dedicated or private because they want the keys never leaving their account.
01:40 Omar Khalil: so host ed with BYOK still has components in redwood's cloud that might see plaintext during processing? i.e. who holds the runtime?
01:50 Priya Nair: hosted runtimes are managed by redwood; with BYOK we do not store your unwrapped key material. that said, the memory during inference will be on managed instances we control. if your requirement is that no third party has access to raw payload and we can't guarantee that, then private on-prem is the only way to fully isolate. dedicated gives you reserved capacity with stronger tenancy and optional VPC peering depending on the cloud provider.
02:15 Luis Ortega: okay, that maps to expectations. our compliance team prefers not to have plain data sitting in a vendor-managed runtime. likely leaning toward Private or on-prem but we need to understand the operational lift and proof points.
02:30 Alex Chen: understood. on proof points — we can share SOC2 Type II report and ISO summary, plus a recent pentest exec summary. i'll attach links after call.
02:42 Dana Park: please.. and can you confirm log delivery? we push all audit logs to our SIEM and we need retention for 12 months, immutable if possible.
02:52 Priya Nair: audit logs can be exported to S3, GCS, or a syslog collector; we support streaming to a customer-owned bucket or pushing via forwarders. retention policy is configurable; default retention in the console is 90 days but for enterprise we can set 365 days and longer with archive tiering. immutability — we can set WORM on your storage side and we include tamper-evident hashes in the log header.
03:18 Jesse Meyers: what about fields — we need user id, request id, model version, prompt hash (not full prompt), response size, latency, and a sla tag.
03:28 Priya Nair: yep we can include all those. note on prompt: for privacy we can do prompt hashing and only store truncated prompt content if you opt in. we can also redaction rules for PII before logs persist.
03:44 Dana Park: ok good. about SSO — we use Okta, need SAML 2.0 with SCIM for group sync and provisioning. also want to map groups to RBAC roles. do you support role mapping?
03:58 Priya Nair: yes — SSO with SAML 2.0 supported across all deployment types. SCIM is supported for hosted and dedicated; for private we can integrate with your SCIM endpoint or offer a proxy. RBAC: we have a role model that supports org/admin/read-only/ops roles and fine-grained permissions around models, rollout, and billing. groups map to roles via claims mapping. we also support custom roles for enterprise.
04:28 Dana Park: how are secrets rotated? KMS lifecycle?
04:34 Priya Nair: rotation depends on KMS. if you use your KMS, you control rotation policy. redwood supports key rotation events and will rewrap data keys as needed. for provider-managed keys we rotate per our internal policy and we share rotation cadence in the security doc.
04:50 Luis Ortega: audit logs + key control addressed. what about RBAC audit trail — we need admin actions to be logged and exportable.
05:02 Priya Nair: admin actions are included in the audit stream — user changes, role grants, model rollouts, and can be forwarded to your SIEM. we include before/after diffs for role changes.
05:18 Omar Khalil: network-wise, if we choose Dedicated, can we do private link/VPC peering and restrict egress? we need to limit outbound access and ensure telemetry goes to our endpoints.
05:28 Priya Nair: yes, dedicated supports VPC peering, private link depending on provider, and egress controls via NAT configuration. for Private deployments we place the control plane in your VPC and you control outbound. for hosted you can set IP allow lists and VPC endpoints for some clouds.
05:48 Dana Park: do you support HSM attestation for key material? we need FIPS 140-2 level 3 or equivalent for some workloads.
05:58 Priya Nair: we integrate with customer HSMs in Private—if you have an HSM-backed KMS we can use those keys. for hosted we use provider-managed HSMs (e.g., cloud HSM) and can provide attestation docs. full FIPS 140-2 Level 3 attestation is possible but often requires private/on-prem with dedicated HSM. we'll need to follow up with our security infra team for exact attest documentation.
06:25 Luis Ortega: timeline — security gate in 8 weeks. we'd like a pilot in prod-ish traffic but limited scope. what kind of telemetry and benchmarks can you run? latency SLOs per token?
06:36 Priya Nair: we publish performance profiles by model and instance type. for pilots we can run a small dedicated pool with reserved capacity and run a latency benchmark against your payload distribution. also can enable KV cache and prefix caching, which reduces token cost.
06:50 Alex Chen: competitors question — are you comparing us to BigCloudAI or EdgeServe?
06:54 Luis Ortega: yeah both — BigCloudAI has a strong managed story, EdgeServe has a good on-prem story. cost and control are the tradeoffs.
07:05 Alex Chen: makes sense. we'll include a short competitive comparison and notes on where Redwood's private and dedicated offerings differ.
07:14 Jesse Meyers: one more legal ask — data residency: our EU customers' data must remain in EU for PII. how strict can you be on region pinning?
07:24 Priya Nair: region pinning is supported in Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be region-restricted but we recommend Dedicated for strict residency SLAs. we'll include an architecture sketch for EU-only deployment.
07:36 Dana Park: can we get a demo of the audit log schema?
07:40 Alex Chen: yes. priya will do the tech deep dive where she'll show sample logs and the delivery pipeline.
07:47 Luis Ortega: ok great. what about retention beyond a year — we might have 3+ years for some data.
07:53 Priya Nair: we support archive policies to cold storage for multi-year retention; retrieval times will be longer but the logs are tamper-evident and we keep checksums.
08:05 Alex Chen: cool — to recap next steps: i'll send SOC2/ISO/pentest artifacts, priya will schedule the tech deep dive and share initial arch diagrams, dana will compile the audit field list, and we'll align on pilot scope and timeline.
08:20 Dana Park: yep, i'll send over a short list today.
08:25 Luis Ortega: thanks all. last question — are there managed key escrow options? if we need a shared recovery mechanism.
08:33 Priya Nair: we do not recommend escrow for production, but for certain enterprise contracts we can set up a dual-control recovery mechanism and escrow via a partner HSM. will need legal signoff.
08:46 Alex Chen: great, we'll follow up in email. thanks everyone.
08:50 (call ends)

Notes: some speaker labels autofilled as "Speaker 6" for legal attendee. Occasional transcription errors: "sock two" instead of SOC2, "sam el" for SAML, "K V cache" for KV cache, minor punctuation.
